_note: Blended USD per million tokens (input + cache + output summed) per model family, fitted to recorded runs.jsonl lines holding usage and a real cost_usd. cost_estimate.py selftest checks it stays within 35 percent per model. usage_input is USD per million input tokens fitted to the host totals in docs/reports/2026-10-07-subagent-mode-live/host-cost.txt (T-0328); usage_multipliers scale it for output, cache read and cache write tokens. usage_calibration (T-0332) multiplies the transcript input and output counts (last line per message id): the host reports input about 200 to 250 times and output about 1.25 times the transcript's (R1 verifier input 260 vs 51956, output 14852 vs 18417; final-rerun verifier input 486 vs 120787, output 20945 vs 27041), while the cache fields match exactly; fitted on those two rows plus the L2 opus verifier, estimate/host 0.83 to 0.93. haiku is scaled from its blended rate, not fitted. haiku is unrefit for Claude Haiku 5.5 (T-0353): both haiku rates were set on the earlier Haiku model, and since then the list price fell from $1 input and $5 output to $0.10 and $0.50 per MTok (prompts up to 100K tokens; $0.50 and $2.50 above; cache read $0.01, cache write 5m $0.125, 1h $0.20) and the newer tokenizer counts about 30 percent more tokens for the same text, so a per-token rate fitted on runs of that model is not comparable and the haiku estimate overstates; one recorded 5.5 run (docs/reports/2026-10-07-haiku-5-5.md) estimated 0.034094 against a host 0.00559, too few rows to refit.
